Thanks again for a productive call earlier today. This thread pulls together the follow-ups and asks we discussed so the team (Redwood + MedTech) can align on an initial operations plan.

High-level recap / asks from Redwood:
- Inventory: please confirm node count, chassis/OEM model, GPU type (incl. VRAM), and current BIOS/firmware baseline we discussed.
- Upgrade cadence & blackout windows: you mentioned monthly maintenance and a 2-week staging test — can you confirm your preferred weekly maintenance window(s)?
- Offline distribution: confirm whether you will provide an internal HTTP repository, or if installers must be supplied via USB/staging server (airgap constraint).
- KMS/HSM: we need to know if you require on-prem HSM integration (KMIP) or if a customer-hosted KMS accessible on the internal network is acceptable.
- On-call & escalation: please share the name/email of the ops lead who will participate in the dry-run and the escalation path for node reboots.

Attachments included: Redwood_Private_Deployment_Checklist_v1.pdf (checklist), POA-draft.docx (initial path-of-action / MAP).

Next steps I propose (pending your answers):
1) MedTech to deliver inventory + maintenance policy by 2026-12-17.
2) Schedule an internal dry-run (Redwood SEs + your ops) w/c 2027-01-24 — target Jan 28 for the first dry-run.
3) PoC week in customer staging (non-prod): target 2027-02-08 to 2027-02-12.
4) Finalize POA and sign before PoC: target 2027-01-15.

If any of that conflicts with your internal constraints, flag it here and we'll adjust.

Thanks Jonas — good summary. Answers inline below.

Inventory / hardware baseline:
- Cluster: 6x Dell PowerEdge R750xa nodes
- GPUs per node: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (kernel 5.15), we run a custom thin-provisioned Ceph backing for model storage
- Current BIOS/firmware: all nodes on iDRAC 4.1.2; GPU firmware 59.22.01

Maintenance windows:
- We have a standing maintenance blackout during M-F 06:00-22:00 local EST; maintenance is normally performed Saturday 01:00–05:00 EST (we prefer this window).
- We test patches in staging for a minimum of 2 weeks before prod promotion.

Offline distribution / staging:
- We cannot accept inbound connections from external internet.
- Preferred: we will host an internal HTTP repository (accessible from the private deployment network) and can pull installer bundles there.
- If needed, we can accept signed bundles via removable media for isolated racks.

KMS/HSM:
- We will use a customer-managed HSM (Thales) accessible only from the internal oracle-vault network. We cannot connect to an external KMS.

On-call & escalation:
- Ops lead for dry-run: Tom Baxter (tom.baxter@medtech.ai). On-call rotation: primary ops engineer 24x7, pager duty available; we will provide the on-call roster prior to the dry-run.

Procurement / timelines:
- PO approval target: 2027-01-20 (internal legal + procurement). Procurement contact: procure@medtech.ai.
- PoC week is fine: Feb 8–12 looks good.

I've attached our maintenance policy for reference (medtech_maintenance_policy.pdf).

—Elena

Hi Elena/Tom — thanks for the quick answers, this is very helpful.
A few technical clarifications from the SE perspective so we can finalize the dry-run MOP:

1) Offline installer distribution
- Internal HTTP repo is ideal — can you confirm basic repo URL and whether access requires client certs? If client certs are required we'll provide signed artifacts and a simple pull script compatible with your repo layout.

2) Expected node outage / rolling strategy
- Our typical rolling patch is designed to keep service online with a per-node restart in the 10–25 minute range (application warm-up and model reload). Can you confirm you have capacity headroom to take 1 node down at a time during the Saturday window? If not, we should plan for a staggered multi-week rollout.

3) Snapshot & DB quiesce
- Do you require a storage snapshot or a quiesce of model-serving processes before restart? If snapshots are required, please share approximate snapshot duration (per node) so we can include it in dry-run timing.

4) Kernel/firmware constraints
- You noted kernel 5.15; our offline bundle includes a kernel-level NIC driver bump for some NIC models — we need confirmation whether you permit that change in staging. If not, we can provide an alternate bundle that only touches userland.

5) KMS/HSM integration
- For KMIP/HSM we will need an endpoint and the CA chain for cert validation. For the dry-run we can run in a simulated mode if you prefer to avoid giving us HSM access in staging.

I've attached an updated offline MOP (offline_mop_v2.txt) that describes the dry-run checklist, expected timings, and rollback steps.

Proposed next actions:
- MedTech: confirm repo URL and whether client certs are needed — target 2026-12-17
- Redwood SEs: prepare alternate non-kernel bundle (if required) — target 2026-12-22
- Schedule dry-run Jan 28 at 01:00–05:00 EST (slot tentative)

If those look good I'll lock the calendar once Jonas confirms the PO/approval targets.

Regards,
